How to Memorize OET Vocabulary Effectively
By Dr. Radwa Elsheikh

Memorizing medical vocabulary for the OET exam can feel overwhelming, but
with the right strategy, it becomes much easier and more effective.
1. Don’t Memorize… Understand
Don’t just memorize the word — understand it.
Example:
“Pleurisy” → in�lammation of the lung lining → causes chest pain

2. Study in Categories (Very Important)
Group words instead of memorizing random lists:
   • Symptoms → pain, swelling, nausea
   • Diseases → asthma, diabetes, pneumonia
   • Jobs → nurse, physiotherapist
   • Treatments → antibiotics, surgery
This helps your brain store information better.

3. Use the 3-Step Revision Rule
   • Day 1 → Learn the word
   • Day 2 → Review it
   • Day 7 → Review again
This is the best way to move words into long-term memory.

4. Use Words in Real Context
Don’t just read — use the word:
    • Make a sentence
    • Imagine a patient case
    • Use it in speaking
Example:
“I’ve been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain.”

5. Focus on High-Yield Words
This �ile includes the most repeated words in OET exams — focus on these
�irst.

6. Learn the Correct Pronunciation �
 
Very important!
   • Always listen to the pronunciation of each word
   • You can use:
         o Google Translate
         o ChatGPT
   • Repeat the word out loud 2–3 times
✔ This improves both listening and Speaking skills.

7. Study Daily (15–20 minutes only)
Consistency is more important than long hours.

� Final Tip:
If you can:
    • Understand the word
    • Pronounce it correctly
    • Use it in a sentence
Then you’ve mastered it ✔


            � Good luck in your OET journey!
                   — Dr. Radwa Elsheikh

How to Memorize OET Vocabulary Effectively
By Dr. Radwa Elsheikh

Memorizing medical vocabulary for the OET exam can feel overwhelming, but
with the right strategy, it becomes much easier and more effective.
1. Don’t Memorize… Understand
Don’t just memorize the word — understand it.
Example:
“Pleurisy” → in�lammation of the lung lining → causes chest pain

2. Study in Categories (Very Important)
Group words instead of memorizing random lists:
   • Symptoms → pain, swelling, nausea
   • Diseases → asthma, diabetes, pneumonia
   • Jobs → nurse, physiotherapist
   • Treatments → antibiotics, surgery
This helps your brain store information better.

3. Use the 3-Step Revision Rule
   • Day 1 → Learn the word
   • Day 2 → Review it
   • Day 7 → Review again
This is the best way to move words into long-term memory.

4. Use Words in Real Context
Don’t just read — use the word:
    • Make a sentence
    • Imagine a patient case
    • Use it in speaking
Example:
“I’ve been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain.”

5. Focus on High-Yield Words
This �ile includes the most repeated words in OET exams — focus on these
�irst.

6. Learn the Correct Pronunciation �

Very important!
   • Always listen to the pronunciation of each word
   • You can use:
         o Google Translate
         o ChatGPT
   • Repeat the word out loud 2–3 times
✔ This improves both listening and Speaking skills.

7. Study Daily (15–20 minutes only)
Consistency is more important than long hours.

� Final Tip:
If you can:
    • Understand the word
    • Pronounce it correctly
    • Use it in a sentence
Then you’ve mastered it ✔


            � Good luck in your OET journey!
                   — Dr. Radwa Elsheikh
